messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: GPU inference queue length > 5m threshold for cluster 'us-west-gpu-1'. Queued requests: 642. Token latency p95 spiking. Incident ID IN-2026-145. Paging on-call

pagerduty: paging alice (oncall-sre) via phone + push :rotating_light:

alice (oncall-sre): on pager, looking. seeing sustained enqueue and 429s from the router. grabbing basics...

ben (infra): I'm up too, checking cluster autoscaler and ASG. any obvious error messages?

alice (oncall-sre): pods stuck Pending in inference namespace. kubectl describe shows events: "FailedCreate: failed to create node: LaunchTemplateVersionMismatch" and cluster-autoscaler logs "scale-up: no compatible node group found". attaching quick snippets:

alice (oncall-sre): ```
$ kubectl get pods -n inference | grep Pending
inference-worker-7f8d9   0/1   Pending   0     12m
inference-worker-8a1c2   0/1   Pending   0     11m
```

ben (infra): running AWS ASG check now. looks like gpu-pool-2 attempted to scale but failed with error from EC2: "The specified Launch Template does not exist (RequestID: ... )". That would explain "no compatible node group" to CA.

carla (ml-op): customer impact: several dedicated tenants are seeing request timeouts and backpressure. Support tickets are flooding in. Sampling logs from the router show 429 throttles for embed and chat endpoints where requests hit the waiting queue.

emily (support): confirmed a named customer (AcmeAI) filed a platform outage ticket, they report 100% of batch jobs failing to start. I've sent them a short note acknowledging and escalating.

alice (oncall-sre): hypothesis: an automated launch-template rotation last night updated the template name/version but the ASG reference wasn't updated. cluster-autoscaler still looking for nodegroup with old launch template id/name so AWS refuses to create new instances. Also noticed node taint changes in new template that CA isn't tolerating.

ben (infra): yep. AWS console shows LaunchTemplate 'redwood-gpu-lt' was replaced by 'redwood-gpu-lt-v2' without updating ASG launch template reference. ASG scale activity shows "Failed to launch instance: Launch Template not found". I can temporarily point ASG to the new LT if we want immediate lift.

carla (ml-op): is there any safe quick mitigation that reduces customer impact while infra fixes template? e.g., diverting lower-priority work to CPU pool or enabling fallback models?

sam (product): we can enable model downgrade for non-prod and lower tier customers, but dedicated contracts might still need GPUs. need to triage which customers to prioritize.

alice (oncall-sre): short mitigation plan: 1) manually scale ASG by updating launch template to correct version and allow create instances (ben) 2) patch cluster-autoscaler nodegroup mapping if node taints differ (alice) 3) temporary routing rule to prioritize tenant IDs in router (sam/emily) 4) monitor queue until back to normal and then rollback any emergency changes.

ben (infra): starting manual ASG update now. I'll change LaunchTemplate specification to redwood-gpu-lt-v2 and request +2 instances.

ben (infra): ```aws autoscaling update-auto-scaling-group --auto-scaling-group-name gpu-pool-2 --launch-template LaunchTemplateId=lt-0abcd1234,Version='$Latest'```

ben (infra): update submitted, requesting immediate instance warmup. AWS reported two instances launched but they fail health checks in ASG because user-data expects a particular AMI tag. investigating.

alice (oncall-sre): cluster-autoscaler logs now show attempts to scale but nodes are coming up NotReady. kubectl describe node shows kubelet failing to start due to missing IAM permissions when trying to attach ENI. error: "UnauthorizedOperation: You are not authorized to perform: ec2:AttachNetworkInterface". that smells like the launch template uses an instance profile missing permissions.

ben (infra): ugh. the new launch template references an instance profile 'redwood-gpu-nodeprofile-v2' that was created without the EC2 network and launch permissions. rollback idea: re-point ASG to previous working launch template (lt-0a1b2c3) and force new instances. but that LT was retired last month.

carla (ml-op): meanwhile queue grows to ~720, tails getting worse. any temporary software-side throttle we can enable to control the queue?

alice (oncall-sre): enabling backpressure on router: set max-concurrency to 200 globally, drop lower priority requests. sam/emily can we publish notice to affected customers?

emily (support): posting to status.redwood.ai with short note that we're investigating GPU capacity issues impacting inference job start times. mention that an on-call engineer is actively working.

sam (product): routing change applied. non-critical tenants will start getting 503s instead of indefinite queue. prioritizing enterprise SLAs for now.

ben (infra): new plan: revert ASG to use an interim launch template that we know has correct instance profile and AMI. creating a temp LT 'redwood-gpu-lt-hotfix' cloning older settings but with latest AMI. will update ASG to point to that.

ben (infra): ```aws ec2 create-launch-template --launch-template-name redwood-gpu-lt-hotfix --version-description hotfix --launch-template-data file://lt-hotfix.json```

ben (infra): ASG updated to use hotfix LT and requested +3 instances. Instances launching...

alice (oncall-sre): nodes coming up. kubelet joins cluster, taints are gpu=true:NoSchedule as expected. cluster-autoscaler recognizes nodes and pods begin scheduling.

carla (ml-op): seeing a drop in queue length to 180 and 429s trending down. nice. continue monitoring.

emily (support): updated AcmeAI with ETA ~20m and that we're provisioning emergency capacity. they acknowledged.

dave (next-oncall): I'm taking handoff. summary: autoscaler failed due to launch template/instance profile mismatch; manual hotfix LT created and ASG updated; nodes added and scheduling resumed; queue draining. I'll keep an eye and follow up with root-cause doc.

alice (oncall-sre): handing to dave for postmortem. please capture timeline, why LT rotation occurred without ASG update, and whether automation needs change to prevent LT renaming without ASG mapping.

dave (next-oncall): will do. immediate next steps: 1) revert router throttles after queue < 50 for 15m (sam) 2) run full cluster-autoscaler and ASG reconciliation script (ben) 3) postmortem and action items assigned.

sam (product): rolling back routing changes now that p95 is back near normal.

carla (ml-op): monitoring long-tail job failures for any pod-level crashes after scheduling. so far stable.

dave (next-oncall): closing incident slack thread when postmortem is published. rough timeline: incident opened 1778851234, ASG hotfix applied ~1778852400, queue under control by 1778854200.

incident-bot: Incident IN-2026-145 status: mitigation in place, monitoring.

alice (oncall-sre): note for postmortem: consider adding a CI check to any launch template rotation that ensures ASG references and instance profiles remain valid. also add CA toleration mapping validation.

emily (support): final customer note drafted, will send when incident declared resolved.

dave (next-oncall): 1778854821 - marking initial mitigation successful. will update with postmortem link later.
